intro: Convert ounces (oz) to pounds (lb) accurately for meat portions, baking ingredients, baby weights, and postal packages. Because one avoirdupois pound equals exactly 16 ounces, each ounce equals 0.0625 pounds—just divide your measurement in ounces by 16. Use the live calculator above for exact decimal pounds, or scan the ounces in a pound chart below for pre-computed weights from 0.5 oz to 600 oz.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Avoirdupois Ounces (oz) vs. Troy Ounces (oz t) vs. Fluid Ounces (fl oz)
items: Standard grocery, meat, and postal scales use the Avoirdupois ounce (1 oz = 28.349523125 g, 16 oz per pound). Gold, silver, and bullion use the Troy ounce (1 oz t = 31.1034768 g, 12 oz t per troy pound).
Do not confuse dry weight ounces (oz) with liquid volume fluid ounces (fl oz); only pure water near standard temperature weighs roughly 1.043 oz per US fl oz.

faqs.question: How many ounces are in a pound of meat (beef, chicken, or pork)?
faqs.answer: There are exactly 16 ounces in 1 pound of meat—whether weighing raw chicken breast, ground beef, or pork. Note that cooked meat yields roughly 12 oz per raw pound after moisture loss, though the 16 oz = 1 lb unit conversion never changes.

faqs.question: How many ounces are in 1 pound (oz in a lb)?
faqs.answer: There are exactly 16 avoirdupois ounces in 1 pound (1 lb = 16 oz), so 1 ounce equals 0.0625 pounds (1 ÷ 16).

faqs.question: How many ounces are in a pound of Freon (refrigerant)?
faqs.answer: There are exactly 16 ounces by weight in a pound of Freon or any other refrigerant. HVAC cylinder charges are measured in standard avoirdupois mass (1 lb = 16 oz), so a 30 lb cylinder holds 480 oz.
